text.p: These are the leading stories in the Belgrade press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified them nor does it vouch for their accuracy.
POLITIKA

- Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic and U.S. envoy John Kornblum said in Belgrade joint efforts for normalisation of realtions in the Balkan region contributed to the strengthening of peace and stabiity in the area.
- The Serbian economy has marked the largest growth in production in Europe this year, Serbian Parliamentary Speaker Dragan Tomic said in Kraljevo.

- German banks Berliner Bank and Deutsche Bank are ready to participate in financing Yugoslav-German trade prior to Yugoslavia's regulation of its IMF membership, says Svetozar Krasin of the Yugoslav Chamber of Commerce.
- First mixed Greek-Yugoslav firm grouping a number of food and beverage companies from the two countries was set up in Kragujevac. Greeks have a 51 percent majority stake in the group.
- The island hotel Sveti Stefan and hotel Milocer on the Montengrin coast will become part of Intercontinental hotels, it was agreed in Budva Tuesday.
- New round of succession talks for the former Yugoslavia in Brussels discusses definition of state property which Yugoslavia considers essential for solving their disputes over succession.

- Belgrade JIK banka a.d. has secured a $70 million credit from the Luxembourg firm Karing holding S.A. It is a 12-year credit with a two-year grace period to be received in 10 monthly installments of five million dollars.
- The second Balkan conference on air line trade unions to be held in Belgrade will discuss opening of Balkan air market and concern over liberalisation of air space.
- Krusik arms factory of Valjevo concludes $3.8 million deal on export of military equipment to a British firm.
- Yugoslavia's trade deficit in first ten months this year is 1.706 billion dollars, says federal statistics office.
- Ruling and opposition parties call on voters to turn out at the run-off elections on November 17.
- Serbian Deputy Prime Minister lays founding stone for building of 7,000 houses in Serb Srarjevo.
- Yugoslavia's first private drug factory opens in Jagodina, starting production with ten lines.
NASA BORBA

- NatWest Markets which was charged with privatising Serbian postal system PTT Serbije has not started the process yet, pending changes to the privatisation and enterprise laws, the paper learns from its London sources.
- The dinar registered a slight drop in its black market exchange rate. The paper speculates on whether banks are behind this
- The Yugoslav Left JUL wants Slobodan Milosevic to be Yugoslavia's president, says head of Belgrade JUL Slobodan Cerovic.
POLITIKA EKSPRES
- Serbian minister of private enterprise Radoje Djukic tenders his resignation citing among other reasons impossible conditions for the private sector.
-- Belgrade Newsroom, 381 11 222 4254
